newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 29.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--The National Bank is examining four different proposals on how to shape its dividend policy for 1997. The proposals on profits, dividends and the distribution of new shares are within the framework of the bank's expansion of its portfolio.

--A new serious of zero coupons will be issued by the finance ministry on January 31. The two-year coupons will have an interest rate of 10.30 percent. Next week, the ministry will hold an auction of one year bills, with date of issue February 5, in an effort to raise 300 billion drachmas.

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis and the national economy and finance ministry are confident that inflation will note a new drop in January, to hover about the 7.0 percent mark. Latest figures indicate it may fall below 7.0 percent.
--Simitis will joint Development Minister Vasso Papandreou in jointly announcing the government's energy, industry, technology and trade policies next week.
IMERISIA

--The series of talks National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou had with the administrations of state-run banks has ended with two decisions: the immediate merger of the Ktimatiki Bank and the National Mortgage Bank; and the appointment of a consultant on the future of the Commercial Bank Group.
--Papandoniou stressed yesterday there were no margins for handouts, in response to the resumption of farmers' protests.
--Stocks continued to rally on the bourse yesterday, closing at 1,149.2 points, an increase of 2.14 percent. Confidence in banks soon passed to construction and insurance. KERDOS
--The government is now approaching problems in the Commercial Bank Group in a different way, wanting to strengthen the Commercial and Ionian Bank's positions.

--The first of 16 new computerised tax department applications will have been installed by April at 132 branches and in all the country's offices by the end of the year. Deputy Foinance Minister George Drys yesterday told Intrasoft the deadline for delivery of the programme was February 28.
--The taxation of state bills and titles is a still a topic of confusion, with differences being noted amongst banks.
EXPRESS
--The second round of the farmers' protests yesterday began with a low profile: both government and farmers, however, say they will not budget from their positions.
--Strikes and labour action will not change the government's economic policy, Papandoniou said following his meeting with Prime Minister Costas Simitis.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--The grading of drachma bonds as A2 by Moody's is an indication of the improvement of economic indicators, the finance ministry believes.
--The share floatation of the Athens Stock Exchange was the main topic at yesterday's meeting with national economy ministry officials.

--OTE, Greece's telecoms organisation, yesterday said it would order software and digital services totalling 20.5 billion drachmas from Siemens and Intracom. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
